axes.model_access: The platform produces no content itself; the evaluation capacity depends on models you configure — LLM-as-a-Judge runs through an "LLM Connection" with credentials you supply (judge doc direct-fetched today). Observed apps can use any framework or model, and self-hosting carries a "Bring your own LLM API" line (self-hosting page fetched today). **The full judge-model list and version mapping were not itemized today — recorded as unknown.**
axes.runtime: Open source and self-deployable (Docker Compose for testing, Kubernetes/Helm for production, per the self-hosting page fetched today), plus an official cloud (AWS US/EU/JP regions, security page fetched today); the interaction surface is a web console with SDKs and an API. **What runs on your machine is the platform service and UI, not the models under evaluation.**
axes.local_files: When self-hosted, traces, scores, prompts and datasets live in your own PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Redis and object storage (fetched today); data arrives via SDK, OpenTelemetry and the API — the platform does not read your local codebase; the export and deletion interface surface was not itemized today.
axes.background: Online evaluation scores production traces asynchronously (evaluation overview and judge docs fetched today); Experiments run datasets in batch. Resume-after-shutdown is not a feature surface for this kind of platform. **Sampling ratios, scoring latency and retry semantics were not verified item by item — recorded as unknown.**
axes.tools: Python and JS SDKs, REST API, OpenTelemetry ingestion; the official documentation MCP server is on record from today's fetch and only exposes docs to agents — whether an authenticated MCP surface can read traces or scores is not verified. CI/CD is used to "block deploys on regressions" (evaluation overview fetched today).
axes.context: Observed objects are organized per project, with traces and scores linked to their source; the four score types NUMERIC, CATEGORICAL, BOOLEAN and TEXT are on record from today; turning traces into datasets and prompt versioning are on the product surface. Cross-project memory is not a platform feature and is not declared by the vendor.
axes.permissions: Self-hosting can be air-gapped so data stays in your environment; the cloud is SOC 2 Type II with project-level RBAC and SSO (security page fetched today). Tier and quota facts (Hobby plus Core, Pro, Enterprise; usage units and data-access windows vary by tier) are on the pricing page from today, with price numbers excluded per D9. **Whether customer data trains models was not found in clause text — recorded as unknown.**
axes.fit: Fits teams that must keep data in their own environment (self-hosted or air-gapped), want observation and evaluation on one trace store, and turn production samples into datasets that block regressions in CI. Not a fit for those who only want a vendor-hosted red-team or compliance-audit service, or who will not bring judge-model credentials. This site does not measure scores and does not rank.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs; conclusions cover the capability and license surfaces only.

**Suggested measurements** (three, each pointing at what the readable official pages do not give):

- Online-evaluation latency and missed coverage: for the same batch of production traces, how long the async judge takes and what the sampling rule is
- The self-hosting upgrade path: migration cost for ClickHouse and object storage when moving from Docker Compose to Helm
- The /ee boundary: which governance and evaluation capabilities exist only in the enterprise directory
unknowns:
- Full judge-model list and version mapping
- Online-evaluation sampling ratio, scoring latency and retry semantics
- The ee/LICENSE text and the enterprise feature boundary it implies
- Whether customer data is used to train models (clause text not read)
- The official changelog page body (404 today; Releases stand in)
- Registry-filing search, and the export/deletion interface inventory
